definition: To make something more noticeable or prominent.
examples: The lighting accentuated her features.
The dress accentuated her slim figure.
His accentuated the positive aspects of the plan.

spanish.definition: Hacer algo más notable o prominente.

definition: To become accustomed to a new climate or environment.
examples: It took weeks to acclimate to the tropical heat.
She quickly acclimated to her new school.
The plants need time to acclimate outdoors.

spanish.definition: Acostumbrarse a un nuevo clima o ambiente.

definition: To approach and address someone boldly or aggressively.
examples: A stranger accosted him on the street.
She was accosted by a salesman at the mall.
He tried to accost the celebrity after the show.

spanish.definition: Abordar y dirigirse a alguien de forma atrevida o agresiva.

definition: To make someone or oneself familiar with something.
examples: You must accustom yourself to the new schedule.
She accustomed her eyes to the darkness.
They accustom themselves to cold weather easily.

spanish.definition: Hacer que alguien se familiarice con algo.

definition: To make someone aware of or familiar with something.
examples: Let me acquaint you with the facts.
She acquainted herself with the new software.
The tour guide acquainted visitors with the history.

spanish.definition: Hacer que alguien conozca o se familiarice con algo.

definition: To make a reality of something; to realize.
examples: She actualized her dream of opening a restaurant.
The plan was actualized after years of effort.
He actualized his potential through hard work.

spanish.definition: Hacer realidad algo; hacer real.

definition: To praise or admire someone excessively.
examples: The fans adulated the rock star wherever he went.
She adulated her mentor beyond reason.
He was adulated by the press for his generosity.

spanish.definition: Alabar o admirar a alguien de manera excesiva.

definition: To make something poorer in quality by adding another substance.
examples: The milk was adulterated with water.
The product was adulterated with cheap fillers.
They were caught adulterating the wine.

spanish.definition: Hacer algo de menor calidad añadiendo otra sustancia.

definition: To cause pain or suffering to someone.
examples: The disease afflicted thousands of people.
Droughts have afflicted the region for years.
She was afflicted with guilt after the argument.

spanish.definition: Causar dolor o sufrimiento a alguien.

definition: To collect or combine into a whole.
examples: The data was aggregated from multiple sources.
The company aggregated its assets over decades.
Scores are aggregated to produce a final ranking.

spanish.definition: Recolectar o combinar en un todo.

definition: To make someone troubled or nervous; to stir up.
examples: The news agitated the public greatly.
She agitated for political reform.
The washing machine agitates the clothes during the cycle.

spanish.definition: Hacer que alguien se sienta inquieto o nervioso.

definition: To place in a straight line or bring into cooperation.
examples: Align the text to the left margin.
The company aligned its goals with market demands.
The troops aligned themselves for inspection.

spanish.definition: Colocar en línea recta o poner en cooperación.

definition: To make suffering or a problem less severe.
examples: The medicine helped alleviate the pain.
Planting trees can alleviate air pollution.
She tried to alleviate his fears with kind words.

spanish.definition: Hacer que el sufrimiento o un problema sea menos severo.

definition: To give or apportion something to someone.
examples: Each student was allotted five minutes to present.
They allotted equal time to each topic.
The budget allotted funds for new equipment.

spanish.definition: Dar o repartir algo a alguien.

definition: To combine or unite to form one structure.
examples: The two companies amalgamated into a single corporation.
Several small towns amalgamated to form one city.
The flavors amalgamated perfectly in the dish.

spanish.definition: Combinar o unir para formar una estructura.

definition: To gather together a large amount of something.
examples: He amassed a fortune through careful investments.
She amassed a collection of over five hundred books.
The army amassed troops at the border.

spanish.definition: Reunir una gran cantidad de algo.

definition: To make something bad or unsatisfactory better.
examples: Steps were taken to ameliorate the living conditions.
The new policy will ameliorate the situation.
They worked tirelessly to ameliorate poverty.

spanish.definition: Hacer que algo malo o insatisfactorio sea mejor.

definition: To make minor changes to improve or correct.
examples: Congress voted to amend the constitution.
She amended her statement to clarify her position.
The committee amended the proposed legislation.

spanish.definition: Hacer cambios menores para mejorar o corregir.

definition: To destroy completely so nothing remains.
examples: The bomb annihilated the entire village.
The army annihilated the opposing forces.
The storm annihilated the coastal town.

spanish.definition: Destruir completamente de modo que no queda nada.

definition: To declare invalid; to cancel officially.
examples: The court annulled the marriage.
The contract was annulled due to fraud.
They sought to annul the previous agreement.

spanish.definition: Declarar inválido; cancelar oficialmente.

definition: To smear with oil as a religious rite; to choose.
examples: The priest anointed the newborn child.
She was anointed as the new leader.
He was anointed with sacred oil during the ceremony.

spanish.definition: Untar con aceite como rito religioso; elegir.

definition: To cause someone to become hostile.
examples: His rude remarks antagonized the entire audience.
Don't antagonize the teacher on the first day.
She antagonized her colleagues with harsh criticism.

spanish.definition: Hacer que alguien se vuelva hostil.

definition: To be earlier than; to precede in time.
examples: This document antedates the official records.
The tradition antedates written history.
The fossils antedate the dinosaur era.

spanish.definition: Ser anterior a; preceder en el tiempo.

definition: To add something at the end of a document or text.
examples: She appended her signature to the letter.
He appended a note to the end of the report.
Additional data was appended to the file.

spanish.definition: Añadir algo al final de un documento o texto.

definition: To assess the value or quality of something.
examples: The expert appraised the painting at fifty thousand.
She appraised the candidates carefully.
The property was appraised for insurance purposes.

spanish.definition: Evaluar el valor o la calidad de algo.

definition: To arrest someone for a crime; to understand.
examples: Police apprehended the suspect within hours.
She apprehended the meaning of his words.
The officer apprehended the fugitive near the border.

spanish.definition: Arrestar a alguien por un crimen; comprender.

She was arraigned before a federal judge.

spanish.definition: Llamar ante un tribunal para responder a una acusación.

examples: She articulated her vision for the company.
He articulated the problem in simple terms.
The speaker articulated each word clearly.

spanish.definition: Expresar ideas de manera clara y efectiva.

definition: To find something out for certain; to determine.
examples: Police tried to ascertain the cause of the fire.
We need to ascertain the facts before proceeding.
She ascertained that the report was accurate.

spanish.definition: Descubrir algo con certeza; determinar.

definition: To make a concerted attack on; to criticize strongly.
examples: The critics assailed the film for its weak plot.
The army assailed the fortress at dawn.
She was assailed by doubts after the meeting.

spanish.definition: Hacer un ataque concertado contra; criticar fuertemente.

definition: To examine or analyze a substance; to attempt.
examples: The lab assayed the ore for gold content.
She assayed to explain the complex theory.
They assayed the water quality carefully.

spanish.definition: Examinar o analizar una sustancia; intentar.

definition: To absorb and integrate information or people.
examples: Students assimilate knowledge through practice.
Immigrants gradually assimilate into the culture.
The body assimilated nutrients from the food.

spanish.definition: Absorber e integrar información o personas.

definition: To classify or arrange things into categories.
examples: She assorted the buttons by color and size.
The candies were assorted in a colorful box.
He sorted and assorted the files meticulously.

spanish.definition: Clasificar o organizar cosas en categorías.

definition: To reduce the force or thickness of something.
examples: The medication attenuated the severity of symptoms.
The signal attenuated over the long distance.
She attenuated her criticism to avoid offense.

spanish.definition: Reducir la fuerza o el grosor de algo.

definition: To provide evidence; to bear witness to.
examples: His record attests to his honesty.
Several witnesses attested to his good character.
The documents attest to the authenticity of the painting.

spanish.definition: Proporcionar evidencia; dar testimonio de.

definition: To regard something as being caused by someone.
examples: She attributed her success to hard work.
The painting is attributed to a famous artist.
They attributed the error to a system glitch.

spanish.definition: Considerar que algo es causado por alguien.

definition: To help or benefit someone.
examples: All his efforts availed him nothing.
She availed herself of the opportunity to study abroad.
The medicine did not avail the patient.

spanish.definition: Ayudar o beneficiar a alguien.

definition: To state or assert to be the case.
examples: He averred that he was completely innocent.
She averred her support for the proposal.
The witness averred that she had seen the incident.

spanish.definition: Declarar o afirmar que algo es el caso.

definition: To prevent something undesirable from happening.
examples: Quick action averted a potential disaster.
She averted her gaze from the gruesome scene.
The government took measures to avert an economic crisis.

spanish.definition: Evitar que algo no deseable suceda.

examples: He avowed his love for her in front of everyone.
She avowed that she would never give up.
They avowed their commitment to peace.

spanish.definition: Afirmar o confesar abiertamente.

definition: To date a document earlier than its actual date.
examples: He backdated the contract to January.
The check was backdated by two weeks.
She backdated the letter to make it seem timely.

spanish.definition: Fechar un documento antes de su fecha real.

definition: To provide the financial backing for something.
examples: Her father bankrolled the startup business.
The government bankrolled the research project.
He bankrolled several independent films.

spanish.definition: Proporcionar el respaldo financiero para algo.

definition: To immerse in water as a religious ceremony.
examples: The baby was baptized in the village church.
She baptized him with a new name.
They baptized the ship with champagne.

spanish.definition: Sumerger en agua como ceremonia religiosa.

definition: To exchange goods or services without money.
examples: They bartered goods at the local market.
She bartered her skills for lodging.
The villagers bartered food for clothing.

spanish.definition: Intercambiar bienes o servicios sin dinero.

examples: The crew battened down the hatches before the storm.

She battened the hatches for the tough times ahead.

spanish.definition: Asegurar con una barra; prepararse para dificultades.

definition: To become friends with someone.
examples: She befriended a fellow student on the first day.
He befriended the elderly neighbor.
They befriended each other during college.

spanish.definition: Hacerse amigo de alguien.

definition: To put someone on a list of people to be punished.
examples: The company blacklisted the unreliable supplier.
She was blacklisted from the industry.
They blacklisted anyone who opposed the regime.

spanish.definition: Poner a alguien en una lista de personas a ser castigadas.

spanish.definition: Agitar un arma u objeto de manera amenazante.

spanish.definition: Tratar a alguien de manera cruel o salvaje.

The developers bulldozed the forest to build houses.

spanish.definition: Limpiar un sitio con un bulldozer; forzar.

She bypassed the usual channels to get results.
The new road bypasses the town completely.

spanish.definition: Ir alrededor o evitar un obstáculo.

definition: To adjust precisely for a particular function.
examples: The technician calibrated the measuring instruments.
She calibrated the scale to ensure accuracy.
The lab calibrated all equipment before the experiment.

spanish.definition: Ajustar con precisión para una función particular.

definition: To declare someone a saint; to glorify.
examples: The church canonized her after her death.
History canonized him as a national hero.
The award canonized her as the best in her field.

spanish.definition: Declarar santo a alguien; glorificar.

definition: To take advantage of something to gain benefit.
examples: She capitalized on her opponent's mistake.
They capitalized on the growing demand for tech.
Investors capitalized on the rising market.

spanish.definition: Aprovechar algo para obtener beneficio.

examples: The small boat capsized in the rough waves.
The canoe capsized but everyone was rescued.
Strong winds capsized several vessels in the harbor.

spanish.definition: Volcar en el agua.

definition: To attract and hold the attention of someone.
examples: The speaker captivated the audience for hours.
Her beauty captivated everyone in the room.
The story captivated readers around the world.

spanish.definition: Atraer y mantener la atención de alguien.

definition: To cause or accelerate a process or change.
examples: The discovery catalyzed a revolution in medicine.
Her speech catalyzed widespread social change.
The event catalyzed investment in the region.

spanish.definition: Causar o acelerar un proceso o cambio.

definition: To place into a particular class or group.
examples: Librarians categorize books by subject.
She categorized the survey responses by age group.
The animals are categorized into different species.

spanish.definition: Colocar en una clase o grupo particular.

They centralized operations to reduce costs.
Power was centralized in the hands of the president.

spanish.definition: Poner bajo un solo control central.

definition: To confirm formally that something is true.
examples: The doctor certified that she was fit to travel.
The product is certified organic by an independent body.
He was certified as a public accountant.

spanish.definition: Confirmar formalmente que algo es verdad.

spanish.definition: Describir el carácter o cualidad de algo.

She chaperoned the teenagers at the party.
The teacher chaperoned the field trip.

spanish.definition: Acompañar y supervisar a alguien en un entorno social.

spanish.definition: Hacer que algo parezca menos valioso o digno.

definition: To name or dedicate something in a ceremony.
examples: They christened the baby at the church.
She christened the ship by breaking champagne.
He christened their new home with a housewarming party.

spanish.definition: Nombrar o dedicar algo en una ceremonia.

definition: To move continuously through an area or system.

The rumor circulated quickly through the office.
Fans circulated through the exhibition halls.

spanish.definition: Moverse continuamente a través de un área o sistema.

examples: They circumvented the regulations through clever loopholes.

spanish.definition: Encontrar una manera de evitar un obstáculo o regla.

examples: We need to clear out the garage this weekend.
She cleared out her desk before leaving the job.
They cleared out the old files from the system.

spanish.definition: Quitar todo y ordenar un espacio.

definition: To come together to form one mass or whole.
examples: The small groups coalesced into a large movement.
Water droplets coalesced on the cold window.
Different ideas coalesced into a unified plan.

spanish.definition: Juntarse para formar una masa o un todo.

definition: To arrange laws or rules into a systematic code.
examples: The committee codified the existing regulations.
She codified the company's informal practices.
The laws were codified into a single document.

spanish.definition: Organizar leyes o reglas en un código sistemático.

definition: To persuade using force or threats.
examples: He was coerced into signing the confession.
She coerced him into revealing the secret.
The gang coerced money from local businesses.

spanish.definition: Persuadir usando fuerza o amenazas.

definition: To collect and combine texts or data in proper order.
examples: She collated the survey results into a report.
The librarian collated the documents carefully.
He collated information from multiple sources.

spanish.definition: Recopilar y combinar textos o datos en orden correcto.

spanish.definition: Enviar colonos y establecer control sobre un territorio.

spanish.definition: Ser correspondiente en tamaño o grado.

spanish.definition: Explotar algo para obtener ganancia comercial.

He commiserated with colleagues who lost their jobs.

spanish.definition: Expresar simpatía o pena por alguien.

examples: She compartmentalized her work and personal life.
The software compartmentalizes data for security.
He compartmentalized his emotions to cope.

spanish.definition: Dividir en secciones o categorías separadas.

spanish.definition: Añadir algo de manera que lo mejora.

spanish.definition: Prensar o apretar algo en un espacio más pequeño.

spanish.definition: Consistir en; estar compuesto de.

Scientists computed the trajectory of the satellite.

spanish.definition: Calcular o determinar una cifra o cantidad.

Scientists conceptualize new theories based on data.

spanish.definition: Formar un concepto o idea de algo.

spanish.definition: Hacer algo más denso o más conciso.

spanish.definition: Aceptar o permitir comportamiento considerado incorrecto.

spanish.definition: Otorgar un título o honor; discutir.

They confided their plans to a trusted advisor.

spanish.definition: Contar a alguien sobre un secreto o asunto privado.

definition: To arrange or set up in a particular form.
examples: She configured the new computer to her preferences.
The software must be configured before first use.
They configured the network for maximum security.

spanish.definition: Organizar o configurar de una forma particular.

The sauce congealed as it cooled down.

spanish.definition: Volverse sólido o semisólido al enfriarse.

definition: To gather into a crowd or mass.

Birds congregated on the power lines at dusk.

spanish.definition: Reunirse en una multitud o masa.

examples: Scientists conjectured that the planet had water.

spanish.definition: Formar una opinión basada en información incompleta.

definition: To make or declare something sacred.
examples: The bishop consecrated the new church.
She consecrated her life to helping the poor.
The ground was consecrated as a memorial.

spanish.definition: Hacer o declarar algo sagrado.

definition: To deliver or hand over to someone's custody.
examples: She consigned the old furniture to the attic.
He was consigned to a life of poverty.
They consigned the artwork to the auction house.

spanish.definition: Entregar o entregar a la custodia de alguien.

definition: To make secret plans jointly to commit an unlawful act.
examples: They conspired to overthrow the government.

She conspired with her colleagues to sabotage the project.

spanish.definition: Hacer planes secretos conjuntos para cometer un acto ilegal.

spanish.definition: Forzar u obligar a alguien a hacer algo.

spanish.definition: Interpretar una palabra o acción de una manera particular.

spanish.definition: Luchar para lidiar con algo difícil.

spanish.definition: Torcer o doblar fuera de su forma normal.

spanish.definition: Reunirse o convocar una reunión.

spanish.definition: Juntarse desde diferentes direcciones para encontrarse.

examples: She conversed with the guests for hours.

He conversed fluently in three languages.

spanish.definition: Participar en un intercambio hablado de pensamientos.

definition: To communicate a message or feeling.
examples: She conveyed her gratitude with a heartfelt letter.

He conveyed the message to the entire team.

spanish.definition: Comunicar un mensaje o sentimiento.

spanish.definition: Tener una relación mutua o recíproca.

definition: To confirm or give support to a statement or theory.

spanish.definition: Confirmar o dar apoyo a una declaración o teoría.

spanish.definition: Destruir gradualmente por acción química.

spanish.definition: Actuar contra algo para reducir su efecto.

He countermanded his earlier instructions.

spanish.definition: Revocar una orden emitiendo una contraria.

examples: The board credentialized all new teachers.

The program credentialized graduates for practice.

spanish.definition: Otorgar credenciales o calificaciones oficiales.

Activists campaigned to criminalize domestic violence.

spanish.definition: Hacer algo ilegal por ley.

examples: The salt crystallized at the bottom of the jar.

spanish.definition: Formar cristales; volverse definido.

definition: To reach a climax or point of highest development.
examples: The festival culminated in a spectacular fireworks display.

spanish.definition: Alcanzar un clímax o punto máximo de desarrollo.

definition: To make or become dark or darker.
examples: The sky darkened as the storm approached.

His expression darkened at the unpleasant news.

spanish.definition: Hacer o volverse oscuro.

spanish.definition: Perder el tiempo siendo lento.

spanish.definition: Hacer que alguien no pueda oír.

spanish.definition: Destruir o matar una gran proporción de.

examples: Organic matter decomposes naturally over time.

Leaves decompose and enrich the soil.

spanish.definition: Descomponerse o causar que se pudra.

definition: To disconnect or separate things that were linked.
examples: The country decoupled its economy from oil dependence.
She decoupled the two railroad cars.
They decoupled growth from environmental damage.

spanish.definition: Desconectar o separar cosas que estaban unidas.

definition: To order something officially by decree.
examples: The king decreed a new tax on imports.
The government decreed a state of emergency.
The court decreed that the law was unconstitutional.

spanish.definition: Ordenar algo oficialmente por decreto.

definition: To publicly denounce or express strong disapproval.
examples: She decried the lack of funding for education.
Activists decried the environmental destruction.
He decried the use of violence in protest.

spanish.definition: Denunciar públicamente o expresar fuerte desaprobación.

definition: To convert encrypted data into readable form.
examples: The spy decrypted the secret message.
She decrypted the file using the password.
It took hours to decrypt the corrupted data.

spanish.definition: Convertir datos cifrados en forma legible.

definition: To arrive at a fact by reasoning.
examples: She deduced from the clues who the murderer was.
We can deduce that the suspect was at the scene.
He deduced the answer through logical reasoning.

spanish.definition: Llegar a un hecho mediante razonamiento.

definition: To take away an amount or part from a total.
examples: They deducted the expenses from her paycheck.
Taxes are deducted automatically from your salary.
She deducted the discount from the total price.

spanish.definition: Quitar una cantidad o parte de un total.

definition: To make or become deep or deeper.
examples: The mystery deepened as new clues emerged.
She deepened her understanding of the subject.
Their friendship deepened over the years.

spanish.definition: Hacer o volverse profundo o más profundo.

definition: To spoil the surface or appearance of something.
examples: Vandals defaced the monument with graffiti.
Someone defaced the painting with red paint.
The inscription was defaced by time and weather.

spanish.definition: Arruinar la superficie o apariencia de algo.

definition: To put off to a later time; to yield respectfully.
examples: They deferred the decision until next month.
She deferred to the expert's opinion.
He deferred his enrollment for a year to travel.

spanish.definition: Postergar para un momento posterior; ceder respetuosamente.

definition: To make dirty or spoil the purity of something.
examples: The army defiled the sacred temple.
He defiled the reputation of the family.
The river was defiled by industrial waste.

spanish.definition: Ensuciar o arruinar la pureza de algo.

definition: To let air or gas out of something.
examples: The balloon slowly deflated after the party.
The central bank deflated the currency.
His ego was deflated by the harsh criticism.

spanish.definition: Dejar salir aire o gas de algo.

definition: To cause to change direction by striking.
examples: The shield deflected the arrow.
She deflected criticism by changing the subject.
The ball deflected off the goalpost.

spanish.definition: Hacer cambiar de dirección al golpear.

definition: To distort the shape or form of something.
examples: The pressure deformed the metal container.
His face was deformed by the injury.
Heat can deform plastic objects.

spanish.definition: Distorsionar la forma de algo.

definition: To provide money to pay a cost or expense.
examples: The grant defrayed the cost of her research.
The company defrayed travel expenses for employees.
Charitable donations defrayed the medical costs.

spanish.definition: Proporcionar dinero para pagar un costo o gasto.

definition: To make a situation less dangerous or tense.
examples: She defused the tense situation with humor.
He defused the bomb with great skill.
The mediator defused the conflict between parties.

spanish.definition: Hacer una situación menos peligrosa o tensa.

definition: To become progressively worse.
examples: The debate degenerated into a shouting match.
His health degenerated rapidly after the diagnosis.
The situation degenerated into chaos.

spanish.definition: Volverse progresivamente peor.

definition: To treat someone with disrespect; to break down.
examples: He degraded his workers with harsh treatment.
The material degrades in sunlight over time.
She refused to degrade herself by begging.

spanish.definition: Tratar a alguien con falta de respeto; descomponer.

definition: To cause to lose a great deal of water.
examples: Hot weather can dehydrate you quickly.
The process dehydrates the fruit for preservation.
Athletes must avoid becoming dehydrated during exercise.

spanish.definition: Hacer perder una gran cantidad de agua.

definition: To entrust a task or responsibility to another.
examples: She delegated the task to her assistant.
A good manager knows when to delegate.
He delegated authority to his deputies.

spanish.definition: Encomendar una tarea o responsabilidad a otro.

definition: To describe or portray something precisely.
examples: The report delineated the key findings clearly.
She delineated the boundaries of the property.
The contract delineates the responsibilities of each party.

spanish.definition: Describir o representar algo con precisión.

definition: To determine the limits or boundaries of something.
examples: The treaty delimited the border between the nations.
She delimitated the scope of the research project.
The law delimits the powers of the government.

spanish.definition: Determinar los límites o fronteras de algo.

definition: To mislead the mind or judgment of someone.
examples: He deluded himself into thinking she loved him.
Don't delude yourself; the task is very difficult.
She was deluded by false promises.

spanish.definition: Engañar la mente o el juicio de alguien.

definition: To remove the magnetic properties of something.
examples: She demagnetized the hard drive before disposing of it.
The device demagnetizes credit cards accidentally.
The scientist demagnetized the sample for the experiment.

spanish.definition: Eliminar las propiedades magnéticas de algo.

definition: To set the boundaries or limits of something.
examples: The fence demarcates the edge of the property.
The agreement demarcated the responsibilities of each party.
Scientists demarcated the different zones of the forest.

spanish.definition: Establecer los límites de algo.

definition: To release from military service.
examples: The troops were demobilized after the war.
The government demobilized thousands of soldiers.
The country demobilized its reserve forces.

spanish.definition: Liberar del servicio militar.

definition: To make something democratic in character.
examples: They worked to democratize the education system.
The internet helped democratize information.
She fought to democratize the organization.

spanish.definition: Hacer algo de carácter democrático.

definition: To cause someone to lose confidence or morale.
examples: The constant setbacks demoralized the team.
She was demoralized by the harsh criticism.
The defeat demoralized the entire army.

spanish.definition: Hacer que alguien pierda confianza o moral.

definition: To move someone to a lower position or rank.
examples: He was demoted from manager to assistant.
She was demoted for poor performance.
The company demoted several executives after the scandal.

spanish.definition: Mover a alguien a una posición o rango inferior.

definition: To transfer from government to private ownership.
examples: The government denationalized several state industries.
They denationalized the airline after years of losses.
The policy denationalized health services.

spanish.definition: Transferir del gobierno a propiedad privada.

definition: To criticize unfairly or disparage.
examples: She denigrated his achievements in front of everyone.
The article denigrated the reputation of the company.
He denigrated his opponents with personal attacks.

spanish.definition: Criticar injustamente o menospreciar.

definition: To give a name to; to express in a particular denomination.
examples: The bonds are denominated in US dollars.
She was denominated as the official candidate.
The currency is denominated in small units.

spanish.definition: Dar un nombre a; expresar en una denominación particular.

definition: To make something less personal or individual.
examples: The automated system depersonalized customer service.
Large hospitals can depersonalize patient care.
The corporate culture depersonalized the workplace.

spanish.definition: Hacer algo menos personal o individual.

definition: To use up the supply or resources of something.
examples: Years of farming depleted the soil nutrients.
The war depleted the country's financial resources.
Overfishing depleted the fish population.

spanish.definition: Usar el suministro o recursos de algo.

definition: To feel or express strong disapproval of something.
examples: She deplored the waste of public funds.
Humanitarians deplored the conditions in the camp.
He deplored the use of violence as a solution.

spanish.definition: Sentir o expresar fuerte desaprobación de algo.

definition: To remove polarization from something.
examples: The new leader depolarized the divided community.
The chemical process depolarized the solution.
They depolarized the political debate.

spanish.definition: Eliminar la polarización de algo.

definition: To reduce the population of an area.
examples: The plague depopulated entire regions of Europe.
War and famine depopulated the countryside.
The epidemic depopulated the small village.

spanish.definition: Reducir la población de un área.

definition: To remove from office suddenly and forcefully.
examples: The military deposed the president in a coup.
She was deposed as CEO after the scandal.
The king was deposed after the revolution.

spanish.definition: Remover del cargo de manera repentina y contundente.

definition: To express disapproval of something.
examples: She deprecated the use of violence in any form.
He deprecated the harsh treatment of prisoners.
The organization deprecated the new policy.

spanish.definition: Expresar desaprobación de algo.

definition: To diminish in value over time.
examples: Cars depreciate rapidly in the first few years.
The currency depreciated against the dollar.
The property depreciated due to the economic downturn.

spanish.definition: Disminuir en valor con el tiempo.

definition: To give someone official authority to act on one's behalf.
examples: She deputized her assistant to sign the documents.
The sheriff deputized several volunteers.
He was deputized to carry a weapon.

spanish.definition: Dar a alguien autoridad oficial para actuar en nombre de uno.

definition: To remove regulations or controls from something.
examples: The government deregulated the airline industry.
They deregulated the telecommunications sector.
The policy deregulated financial markets.

spanish.definition: Eliminar regulaciones o controles de algo.

definition: To express contempt for; to ridicule.
examples: The critics derided the film as amateurish.
She derided his ideas as impractical.
He was derided for his unusual fashion sense.

spanish.definition: Expresar desprecio; ridiculizar.

definition: To make someone less sensitive to something.
examples: Violent movies can desensitize young viewers.
The medication desensitized the nerve endings.
Repeated exposure desensitized them to the pain.

spanish.definition: Hacer a alguien menos sensible a algo.

definition: To appoint someone to a specified position.
examples: She was designated as the team leader.
The area was designated as a protected wildlife zone.
He designated his wife as the beneficiary.

spanish.definition: Nombrar a alguien para una posición especificada.

definition: To make a place deserted or barren.
examples: The war desolated the once beautiful countryside.
She felt desolate after losing her job.
The storm desolated the small farming community.

spanish.definition: Hacer que un lugar esté desierto o estéril.

definition: To upset the stability of something.
examples: The scandal destabilized the government.
The policy destabilized the financial markets.
His behavior destabilized the entire team.

spanish.definition: Alterar la estabilidad de algo.

definition: To abolish the segregation of people.
examples: The schools were desegregated in the nineteen sixties.
They desegregated the military after the war.
The law desegregated public facilities.

spanish.definition: Abolir la segregación de personas.

definition: To become progressively worse.
examples: His health deteriorated rapidly after the diagnosis.
The building deteriorated over the years.
Relations between the countries deteriorated sharply.

spanish.definition: Volverse progresivamente peor.

definition: To dislike something intensely.
examples: She detested the taste of cilantro.
He detested being told what to do.
They detested the noise from the construction.

spanish.definition: No gustar algo de manera intensa.

definition: To explode or cause to explode.
examples: The bomb detonated at noon.
She detonated the charges remotely.
The device failed to detonate properly.

spanish.definition: Explotar o causar que explote.

definition: To reduce the value or worth of something.
examples: The country devalued its currency to boost exports.
She felt her contributions were devalued.
Inflation devalued their savings over time.

spanish.definition: Reducir el valor o la importancia de algo.

definition: To recognize or ascertain what makes something different.
examples: Can you differentiate between the two species?
The company differentiates itself through quality.
She differentiated the main points clearly.

spanish.definition: Reconocer o determinar lo que hace algo diferente.

definition: To spread or cause to spread widely.
examples: The scent diffused through the entire room.
The light diffused softly through the curtains.
Information diffused quickly through the network.

spanish.definition: Extender o causar que se extienda ampliamente.

definition: To break down food in the body; to absorb information.
examples: It takes hours to digest a heavy meal.
She needed time to digest the information.
The body digests proteins into amino acids.

spanish.definition: Descomponer alimentos en el cuerpo; absorber información.

definition: To confer dignity or honor upon someone.
examples: She dignified the occasion with her presence.
He dignified the small ceremony with a speech.
They dignified the event by attending in person.

spanish.definition: Conferir dignidad u honor a alguien.

definition: To make a liquid weaker by adding water.
examples: Dilute the paint with a small amount of water.
They diluted the strength of the proposal.
The juice was diluted to reduce sweetness.

spanish.definition: Hacer un líquido más débil añadiendo agua.

definition: To take a machine or structure to pieces.
examples: She disassembled the engine to find the problem.
They disassembled the furniture for the move.
He disassembled the device carefully.

spanish.definition: Desarmar una máquina o estructura en piezas.

definition: To cause a group to break up and stop functioning.
examples: The band disbanded after their final tour.
The committee disbanded after completing the project.
The crowd was ordered to disband by police.

spanish.definition: Hacer que un grupo se separe y deje de funcionar.

definition: To pay out money from a fund.
examples: The bank disbursed the loan funds promptly.
The government disbursed emergency relief aid.
Funds were disbursed to the affected families.

spanish.definition: Pagar dinero de un fondo.

definition: To perceive or recognize something clearly.
examples: She could discern a hint of sadness in his voice.
It was hard to discern the truth from the lies.
He discerned a pattern in the data.

spanish.definition: Percibir o reconocer algo claramente.

definition: To stop doing or providing something.
examples: The company discontinued the unpopular product.
She discontinued her medication without consulting her doctor.
They discontinued service to the remote area.

spanish.definition: Dejar de hacer o proporcionar algo.

definition: To make an unjust distinction in the treatment of people.
examples: It is illegal to discriminate based on race.
She could discriminate between the two shades of blue.
The law prohibits employers from discriminating against workers.

spanish.definition: Hacer una distinción injusta en el trato de personas.

definition: To consider something unworthy of consideration.
examples: She disdained his offer of help.
He disdained the cheap furniture in the apartment.
They disdained the notion of asking for help.

spanish.definition: Considerar algo indigno de consideración.

definition: To leave a ship, aircraft, or other vehicle.
examples: Passengers disembarked at the port.
We disembarked from the flight at dawn.
The troops disembarked on the enemy shore.

spanish.definition: Salir de un barco, avión u otro vehículo.

definition: To deprive someone of a right or privilege.
examples: The law disenfranchised thousands of voters.
Policies that disenfranchise the poor are unjust.
They were disenfranchised from the political process.

spanish.definition: Privar a alguien de un derecho o privilegio.

definition: To disconnect or release from something engaged.
examples: She disengaged the clutch and shifted gears.
He disengaged himself from the toxic relationship.
The mechanism disengaged automatically.

spanish.definition: Desconectar o liberar de algo conectado.

definition: To spoil the appearance of something.
examples: The accident disfigured her face permanently.
Vandalism disfigured the beautiful sculpture.
The scar disfigured his once handsome face.

spanish.definition: Arruinar la apariencia de algo.

definition: To discharge or vomit something; to yield.
examples: The river disgorged into the ocean.
The company disgorged its profits to shareholders.
The pipe disgorged thick black smoke.

spanish.definition: Descargar o vomitar algo; producir.

definition: To cause someone to lose determination or confidence.
examples: The rejection disheartened her deeply.
She was disheartened by the lack of progress.
Nothing disheartened his optimistic spirit.

spanish.definition: Hacer que alguien pierda determinación o confianza.

definition: To deprive someone of an inheritance.
examples: He disinherited his eldest son from the will.
She was disinherited after the family dispute.
The father disinherited all his children.

spanish.definition: Privar a alguien de una herencia.

definition: To break up into small parts; to fall apart.
examples: The old building disintegrated over the decades.
The spacecraft disintegrated upon re-entry.
His alibi disintegrated under questioning.

spanish.definition: Romperse en partes pequeñas; desmoronarse.

definition: To free from false belief or naive expectations.
examples: The experience disillusioned her about politics.
He became disillusioned with the corporate world.
The scandal disillusioned many loyal supporters.

spanish.definition: Liberar de una creencia falsa o expectativas ingenuas.

definition: To clean something to prevent infection.
examples: She disinfected the wound before bandaging it.
They disinfected the hospital rooms thoroughly.
Please disinfect your hands before entering.

spanish.definition: Limpiar algo para prevenir infecciones.

definition: To dig up something that has been buried.
examples: The body was disinterred for further examination.
They disinterred the time capsule from the garden.
Authorities disinterred the remains for DNA testing.

spanish.definition: Desenterrar algo que ha sido enterrado.

definition: To force a bone out of its normal position.
examples: She dislocated her shoulder during the fall.
The earthquake dislocated the water supply system.
The accident dislocated his knee badly.

spanish.definition: Forzar un hueso fuera de su posición normal.

definition: To force something out from a fixed position.
examples: Water dislodged the stuck pebble from the drain.
The impact dislodged several teeth.
Firefighters dislodged the debris blocking the entrance.

spanish.definition: Forzar algo fuera de una posición fija.

definition: To take a machine or structure to pieces.
examples: Workers dismantled the old bridge carefully.
The company dismantled its overseas operations.
They dismantled the nuclear weapons program.

spanish.definition: Desarmar una máquina o estructura en piezas.

definition: To disrupt the organization of something.
examples: The power outage disorganized the entire operation.
She disorganized his files by accident.
The storm disorganized the carefully planned schedule.

spanish.definition: Interrumpir la organización de algo.

definition: To regard or represent as being of little worth.
examples: She disparaged his efforts at every opportunity.
He disparaged the work of his competitors.
They disparaged the quality of the local product.

spanish.definition: Considerar o representar como de poco valor.

definition: To make a feeling or belief disappear.
examples: The evidence dispelled all doubts about his guilt.
Sunlight dispelled the morning fog.
Her kind words dispelled my fears.

spanish.definition: Hacer que un sentimiento o creencia desaparezca.

definition: To cause someone to feel annoyed or dissatisfied.
examples: His tardiness displeased the strict teacher.
The results displeased the board of directors.
She was displeased with the quality of service.

spanish.definition: Hacer que alguien se sienta molesto o insatisfecho.

definition: To deprive someone of land or property.
examples: The war dispossessed thousands of families.
They were dispossessed of their ancestral land.
The government dispossessed the farmers without compensation.

spanish.definition: Privar a alguien de tierras o propiedad.

definition: To conceal one's true motives or feelings.
examples: She dissembled her true feelings behind a smile.
He dissembled about his involvement in the scandal.
They dissembled their intentions to gain trust.

spanish.definition: Ocultar los verdaderos motivos o sentimientos.

definition: To spread information widely.
examples: The organization disseminated the report to all members.
She disseminated her research findings widely.
The government disseminated public health information.

spanish.definition: Distribuir información ampliamente.

definition: To hold or express opinions that differ from official ones.
examples: She dissented from the majority opinion.
Several judges dissented from the ruling.
He dissented against the party line.

spanish.definition: Mantener o expresar opiniones diferentes de las oficiales.

definition: To disconnect or separate from association.
examples: She dissociated herself from the controversial statement.
He dissociated from his former political allies.
The company dissociated from the activist group.

spanish.definition: Desconectar o separar de una asociación.

definition: To persuade someone not to do something.
examples: She dissuaded him from quitting his job.
Nothing could dissuade her from pursuing her dream.
He tried to dissuade them from traveling alone.

spanish.definition: Persuadir a alguien de no hacer algo.

definition: To cause to become separated or divided.
examples: The disagreement disunited the political party.
Personal conflicts disunited the once close team.
They were disunited by ideological differences.

spanish.definition: Hacer que se separen o dividan.

definition: To separate from another route or path.
examples: The road diverges into two paths ahead.
Their opinions diverged on the key issue.
The two theories diverge in their fundamental assumptions.

spanish.definition: Separarse de otra ruta o camino.

definition: To make something more varied or diverse.
examples: The company diversified its product line.
She diversified her investment portfolio.
Farmers diversified their crops to reduce risk.

spanish.definition: Hacer algo más variado o diverso.

definition: To deprive someone of power or possessions.
examples: The company divested its noncore assets.
He was divested of his authority.
She divested herself of all worldly possessions.

spanish.definition: Privar a alguien de poder o posesiones.

definition: To tame an animal for human use.
examples: Humans domesticated dogs thousands of years ago.
She domesticated wild plants for her garden.
The culture domesticated the horse for transport.

spanish.definition: Domar un animal para uso humano.

definition: To lower in rank or importance.
examples: She was downgraded from first class to economy.
The credit rating agency downgraded the country's debt.
They downgraded the severity of the warning.

spanish.definition: Bajar de rango o importancia.

definition: To make something appear less important.
examples: She downplayed her role in the project's success.
The company downplayed the severity of the data breach.
He downplayed his injury to stay in the game.

spanish.definition: Hacer que algo parezca menos importante.

definition: To reduce the number of employees in a company.
examples: The company downsized by laying off two hundred workers.
They downsized their operations to cut costs.
The firm downsized its office space after the merger.

spanish.definition: Reducir el número de empleados en una empresa.

definition: To clean out the bed of a river or harbor.
examples: Workers dredged the harbor to allow larger ships.
She dredged up old memories during the interview.
They dredged the lake bottom for artifacts.

spanish.definition: Limpiar el lecho de un río o puerto.

definition: To give an unofficial name or nickname to someone.
examples: She was dubbed the 'Queen of Pop' by the media.
They dubbed the new building the Tower.
The film was dubbed into several languages.

spanish.definition: Dar un nombre o apodo no oficial a alguien.

definition: To designate something for a specific purpose.
examples: The funds were earmarked for education spending.
She earmarked the book for the library donation.
Resources were earmarked for disaster relief.

spanish.definition: Designar algo para un propósito específico.

definition: To spend money or use resources carefully.
examples: We need to economize during the recession.
She economized by cooking at home instead of dining out.
They economized on fuel by carpooling.

spanish.definition: Gastar dinero o usar recursos cuidadosamente.

definition: To erase or remove a mark or memory.
examples: Time effaced the painful memories.
She effaced herself from the group photo.
The rain effaced the chalk drawings on the sidewalk.

spanish.definition: Borrar o eliminar una marca o recuerdo.

definition: To bring about or put into effect.
examples: She effectuated the changes in company policy.
They effectuated the merger last month.
The government effectuated new trade regulations.

spanish.definition: Llevar a cabo o poner en efecto.

definition: To give off bubbles; to show excitement.
examples: The champagne effervesced in the glass.
She effervesced with joy at the news.
The drink effervesced when the tablet was added.

spanish.definition: Emitir burbujas; mostrar emoción.

definition: To utter a sudden cry or exclamation.
examples: He ejaculated with surprise when he saw the gift.
She ejaculated a warning to the children.
The crowd ejaculated cheers at the victory.

spanish.definition: Pronunciar un grito o exclamación repentina.

definition: To pass or go by in reference to time.
examples: Several weeks elapsed before she responded.
Three years have elapsed since we last met.
Time elapsed quickly during the vacation.

spanish.definition: Pasar o transcurrir en referencia al tiempo.

definition: To evoke or draw out a response or answer.
examples: The question elicited a strong emotional response.
She elicited valuable information from the witness.
The joke elicited laughter from the audience.

spanish.definition: Provocar o extraer una respuesta o respuesta.

definition: To evade or escape from someone or something.
examples: The suspect eluded police for several days.
Success eluded her for many years.
The answer eluded him despite careful thought.

spanish.definition: Evitar o escapar de alguien o algo.

definition: To set free from legal, social, or political restrictions.
examples: The proclamation emancipated millions of enslaved people.
She emancipated herself from her family's control.
The law emancipated minors under certain conditions.

spanish.definition: Liberar de restricciones legales, sociales o políticas.

definition: To fix something firmly and deeply in a surrounding mass.
examples: The reporter was embedded with the military unit.
She embedded the sensor in the concrete.
The journalist was embedded with troops during the conflict.

spanish.definition: Fijar algo firmemente en una masa circundante.

definition: To make something more attractive by adding decorations.
examples: She embellished the dress with sequins and beads.
He embellished the story with fictional details.
They embellished the hall with flowers and lights.

spanish.definition: Hacer algo más atractivo añadiendo decoraciones.

definition: To steal money entrusted to one's care.
examples: The accountant embezzled thousands from the company.
She embezzled funds over a period of five years.
He was arrested for embezzling client money.

spanish.definition: Robar dinero confiado al cuidado de uno.

definition: To give someone courage or confidence.
examples: The success emboldened her to try again.
She was emboldened by the support of her friends.
The victory emboldened the troops to advance.

spanish.definition: Dar valor o confianza a alguien.

definition: To be an expression of or give a visible form to an idea.
examples: She embodies the values of the organization.
The constitution embodies the will of the people.
The character embodies the spirit of rebellion.

spanish.definition: Ser una expresión o dar forma visible a una idea.

definition: To decorate fabric with needlework; to embellish.
examples: She embroidered flowers on the pillowcase.
He embroidered his account of the adventure.
The artisan embroidered intricate patterns on the fabric.

spanish.definition: Decorar tela con bordados; embellecer.

definition: To leave one's own country to settle permanently in another.
examples: Her family emigrated from Italy to America.
They emigrated to escape political persecution.
Millions emigrated during the great famine.

spanish.definition: Salir de su propio país para establecerse permanentemente en otro.

definition: To understand and share the feelings of another.
examples: She empathized with the grieving family.
It is hard to empathize with someone you have never met.
He empathized deeply with the characters in the novel.

spanish.definition: Entender y compartir los sentimientos de otro.

definition: To match or surpass by imitation.
examples: She emulated her mentor's success in science.
He emulated the style of the great masters.
The company emulated its competitor's successful strategy.

spanish.definition: Igualar o superar mediante imitación.

definition: To fill with love or delight.
examples: She was enamored with the charming old town.
He became enamored of the idea of starting a business.
They were enamored by the beauty of the landscape.

spanish.definition: Llenar de amor o deleite.

definition: To express the essential features of something succinctly.
examples: The title encapsulates the main theme of the book.
She encapsulated her philosophy in one sentence.
The technology encapsulates the medicine for slow release.

spanish.definition: Expresar las características esenciales de algo.

definition: To enclose something in a covering or case.
examples: The fossil was encased in solid rock.
Her leg was encased in a plaster cast.
The diamond was encased in an elaborate setting.

spanish.definition: Intrudir en el territorio o derechos de una persona.

spanish.definition: Convertir información en un código secreto.

spanish.definition: Pesado o cargar a alguien o algo.

spanish.definition: Poner a alguien o algo en riesgo de daño.

spanish.definition: Declarar la aprobación o apoyo público.

spanish.definition: Dar vitalidad y entusiasmo a alguien.

spanish.definition: Cortar o tallar un diseño en una superficie dura.

spanish.definition: Absorber toda la atención o interés de alguien.

spanish.definition: Inscribirse o ser inscrito en las fuerzas armadas.

spanish.definition: Hacer algo más entretenido o interesante.

spanish.definition: Hacer a alguien o algo más noble en carácter.

The relics were enshrined in the temple.

spanish.definition: Preservar algo en un lugar de honor.

spanish.definition: Suceder u ocurrir después o como resultado.

spanish.definition: Torcer juntos; involucrar en dificultad.

spanish.definition: Capturar la atención fascinada de alguien.

spanish.definition: Hablar sobre algo con gran emoción.

spanish.definition: Atraer o tentar ofreciendo algo agradable.

spanish.definition: Dar a alguien el derecho de hacer o tener algo.

spanish.definition: Colocar en o como en una tumba.

spanish.definition: Dar a alguien la responsabilidad de algo.

spanish.definition: Torcer o enrollar juntos.

spanish.definition: Mencionar varias cosas una por una.

spanish.definition: Decir o pronunciar con claridad.

spanish.definition: Contemplar o concebir como una posibilidad.

spanish.definition: Ser un ejemplo perfecto de algo.

spanish.definition: Hacer las cosas iguales en cantidad o estado.

spanish.definition: Considerar una cosa como la misma o equivalente a otra.

spanish.definition: Destruir completamente; poner fin a.

spanish.definition: Estallar violentamente, especialmente un volcán.

spanish.definition: Volverse o causar que se vuelva más intenso.

spanish.definition: Evitar deliberadamente o abstenerse de.

spanish.definition: Adoptar o apoyar una causa, creencia o forma de vida.

spanish.definition: Tener en alta estima o favorable; respetar.

spanish.definition: Cortar o tallar un diseño en una superficie con ácido.

spanish.definition: Hablar o escribir en alta alabanza de alguien.

spanish.definition: Cambiar de un líquido a un vapor.

spanish.definition: Suceder u ocurrir como resultado.

spanish.definition: Empeorar un problema o situación mala.

spanish.definition: Irritar intensamente; enfurecer.

spanish.definition: Hacer un hoyo quitando tierra.

spanish.definition: Tomar un extracto corto de un texto o película.

spanish.definition: Gritar de repente, especialmente de sorpresa.

spanish.definition: Excluir oficialmente a alguien de una comunidad religiosa.

spanish.definition: Descargar materia de desecho del cuerpo.

spanish.definition: Capaz de ser transmitido o comunicado.

definition: Friendly, lively, and enjoyable.
examples: The party had a convivial atmosphere.
They enjoyed a convivial dinner together.
The convivial host made everyone feel at ease.

spanish.definition: Amistoso, animado y agradable.

definition: Extremely complex and difficult to follow.
examples: The plot was convoluted and hard to follow.
He gave a convoluted explanation of the problem.
The convoluted legal process frustrated everyone.

spanish.definition: Extremadamente complejo y difícil de seguir.

definition: Abundant in supply or quantity.
examples: She took copious notes during the lecture.
The rain produced copious amounts of water.
He had copious amounts of evidence.

spanish.definition: Abundante en suministro o cantidad.

definition: In a fluent and coherent manner.
examples: She articulated her views articulately.
He spoke articulately about the complex issue.
The speaker argued articulately for reform.

spanish.definition: De manera fluida y coherente.

definition: With great care and perseverance.
examples: She worked assiduously on the research project.
He assiduously followed the doctor's advice.
They assiduously pursued the goal for years.

spanish.definition: Con gran cuidado y perseverancia.

definition: In a bold or daring way.
examples: She audaciously challenged the status quo.
He audaciously proposed a radical new idea.
They audaciously attempted the impossible.

spanish.definition: De manera audaz o atrevida.

definition: In a way that produces good results.
examples: The new policy affected citizens beneficially.
Exercise beneficially impacts mental health.
The treatment beneficially changed his condition.

spanish.definition: De una manera que produce buenos resultados.

definition: In a cruel and insensitive way.
examples: He callously ignored her pleas for help.
She callously dismissed their concerns.
They callously exploited the workers.

spanish.definition: De una manera cruel e insensible.

definition: In a way that relates to the sky or heavens.
examples: The lights shone celestially in the night sky.
She gazed celestially at the stars above.
The phenomenon occurred celestially once a century.

spanish.definition: De una manera relacionada con el cielo o los cielos.

definition: In a way that settles an issue decisively.
examples: The evidence conclusively proved his guilt.
She conclusively demonstrated the theory.
The test conclusively showed the results.

spanish.definition: De una manera que resuelve una cuestión decisivamente.

definition: Subject to certain requirements being met.
examples: She was conditionally released from prison.
The offer was conditionally accepted.
They conditionally agreed to the terms.

spanish.definition: Sujeto a que se cumplan ciertos requisitos.

definition: In a way that makes an outcome likely.
examples: The environment was not conducive to studying.
She arranged the room conducive to work.
The atmosphere was conducive to relaxation.

spanish.definition: De una manera que hace probable un resultado.

definition: In a way that shows deep disrespect.
examples: She contemptuously dismissed his suggestion.
He contemptuously sneered at the idea.
They contemptuously rejected the proposal.

spanish.definition: De una manera que muestra profundo irrespeto.

definition: In a way that is likely to cause argument.
examples: The issue was contentiously debated.
They contentiously argued over the details.
He contentiously raised the objection.

spanish.definition: De una manera que probablemente causa argumento.

definition: In a friendly and enjoyable manner.
examples: They convivially shared stories over dinner.
She convivially welcomed every guest.
They spent the evening convivially together.

spanish.definition: De una manera amistosa y agradable.

definition: An intense enthusiasm for a short period.
examples: The latest dance craze swept the nation.
The fad was a brief craze that quickly faded.
The toy was the craze of the holiday season.

spanish.definition: Un entusiasmo intenso por un corto período.

definition: A tendency to be too ready to believe something.
examples: His credulity made him an easy target for scams.
She was shocked by his incredible credulity.
The public's credulity was exploited by con artists.

spanish.definition: La tendencia a estar demasiado listo para creer algo.

definition: A system of beliefs or principles.
examples: The religious creed was recited every Sunday.
He lived by a simple personal creed.
The political creed guided their actions.

spanish.definition: Un sistema de creencias o principios.

definition: A narrow opening resulting from a split or crack.
examples: The small plant grew from a crevice in the rock.
Water seeped through every crevice in the dam.
She spotted the lizard hiding in a crevice.

spanish.definition: Una abertura estrecha resultado de una división o grieta.

definition: A standard by which something may be judged.
examples: What criterion did you use to select the winner?
The main criterion is academic excellence.
We need clear criteria for evaluation.

spanish.definition: Un estándar por el cual algo puede ser juzgado.

definition: A detailed analysis and assessment of something.
examples: She wrote a thorough critique of the novel.
The professor's critique was harsh but fair.
The film received positive critiques from reviewers.

spanish.definition: Un análisis y evaluación detallados de algo.

definition: A place of severe test or trial.
examples: The war was a crucible that tested the nation's resolve.
The competition served as a crucible for young talent.
He emerged from the crucible of adversity stronger.

spanish.definition: Un lugar de prueba o ensayo severo.

definition: A vigorous campaign for political, social, or religious change.
examples: She led a crusade against corporate corruption.
The civil rights movement was a great crusade.
His crusade for reform inspired many followers.

spanish.definition: Una campaña vigorosa por cambio político, social o religioso.

definition: An underground room or vault for burial.
examples: The ancient crypt beneath the church was preserved.
The family was buried in a private crypt.
Archaeologists explored the crypt carefully.

spanish.definition: Una habitación subterránea o bóveda para entierro.

definition: The highest point; the climax.
examples: The award was the culmination of her career.
The festival reached its culmination with fireworks.
The project was the culmination of years of work.

spanish.definition: El punto más alto; el clímax.

definition: Having a tendency to be too ready to believe.
examples: The credulous man fell for every scam.
She was too credulous to question his story.
Credulous audiences believe everything they see on TV.

spanish.definition: Que tiene tendencia a creer demasiado fácilmente.

definition: Having a meaning that is mysterious or obscure.
examples: She left a cryptic note on the table.
His cryptic remarks puzzled everyone.
The ancient text contained cryptic symbols.

spanish.definition: Que tiene un significado misterioso u oscuro.

definition: Hasty and therefore not thorough or detailed.
examples: She gave the report only a cursory glance.
A cursory inspection revealed no obvious problems.
He made a cursory attempt to clean the house.

spanish.definition: Rápido y por lo tanto no exhaustivo ni detallado.

definition: Greed for money or possessions; avarice.
examples: His cupidity led him to embezzle from the company.
The cupidity of the corrupt officials was staggering.
Greed and cupidity drove many of the characters in the novel.

spanish.definition: Codicia por dinero o posesiones; avaricia.
